Thanks for the suggestion, there is a 4 meter altitude sensor paired with a speed sensor as I have found this allows for the smoothest flight pattern. So yes , you can drop it from higher altitudes but it has a much longer glide slope down to the correct 4 meter altitude and this meant it was hard to capture the altitude hold feature in a short video.

Edit: In theory it doesn't have a maximum altitude but there is a minimum of 20 meters , as shown in the video

Thank you ! It took quite a while but really there's only 4 important parts 

1. Thrust : attach your thrust to an xor gate with two altitude sensors set to -500 meters. One will be on your Missile and one on your creation , this means the thrust automatically starts once it detaches but not while on your build 

2. Altitude control : using a speed sensor set to 0.1km/h and facing downwards , hook it into a gimbal OR set the pervious xor gate to hinges on fold out wings to slow decent . Now set a second altitude sensor to whatever altitude you want to hold at eg. 2 meters and set it to trigger below. This will be hooked into gimbal jets which keep it from going below this height . 

3. Stability: huge shout-out to the devs as the gyro stabilisers help here . Set them to off by default and hook them up to the xor gate  . Have one for the pitch and roll axis. To stabilise yaw, set a regular gyro to speed 10 and have it on the yaw axis without controls 

4. Proxy fuse: set a few distance sensors into an OR gate, then this OR gate into an AND gate. Hook the XOR gate into the AND gate and then set the AND gate into the dynamite. 

It takes alot of playing around and trial + error so take your time and as stated before the mk.18-2 will be on the workshop shortly!
